guides/job-limits.mdx.review_opus_note: The "Maximum executions" section contains a hallucinated exemption: the Arabic adds a parenthetical "(يمكن تقسيم مهام Estimator إلى مهام فرعية أصغر، لذا لا ينطبق هذا الحد عليها)" — "Estimator jobs can be split into smaller sub-jobs, so this limit does not apply to them" — which appears nowhere in the English, and at the same time it deletes the source's actual justification, "due to output size". A learner reading the Arabic would conclude the 10-million-execution cap simply does not govern Estimator workloads and would size Estimator jobs accordingly; that is a false belief about a hard service limit, so it is misleading, not merely stylistic. Separately, the intro strengthens the English hedge "to decrease the likelihood that your job fails after you've waited for it to go through the queue" into an absolute "لتجنب انتظارها في الطابور ثم فشلها في النهاية" (to avoid it queuing and then failing), turning a probabilistic claim into a guarantee. Terminology is otherwise sound and consistent (كيوبت, بوابات ثنائية الكيوبت, اللقطات for shots), and the instruction-count table and per-qubit section are faithful; the only stylistic wart is the doubled "ذات صلة بحد [الحد الأقصى..." in the admonition.

learning/courses/basics-of-quantum-infor.review_notes: Technical accuracy preserved
learning/courses/basics-of-quantum-infor.review_opus_note: The physics is faithful throughout — the four measurement branches (00→nothing, 01→Z, 10→X, 11→ZX), the classical-control note, the "e-bit is burned" cost, and the no-cloning argument all map exactly onto the English, and the informal register (لاحظ، تصوّر) holds. The substantive slip is "an arbitrary quantum state" rendered as "حالة كمية عشوائية" (= a *random* state) in the identity-operation argument (line 309); the whole force of that argument is that it holds for ANY state, so "عشوائية" softens a universal claim into a probabilistic one — it should be "حالة كمية اعتباطية/أي حالة كمية". learning/courses/variational-algorithm-d.review_opus_note: The core term "observable" is rendered throughout as "متغيّر" (= variable / variant), roughly ten times (lines 50, 162, 205, 256, 293, 310, 329, 348, 464), which teaches a false concept: an observable is a Hermitian operator, not a variable, and this lesson is entirely about estimating expectation values of one. The damage is compounded because "متغيّر" is simultaneously the file's word for "variant" — line 205 reads "هو متغيّر من VQE ... أول k قيم ذاتية لمتغيّر Ĥ", using the same word for "variant of VQE" and for "observable Ĥ" in one sentence, so the concept becomes unidentifiable; line 297 ("الحالات الذاتية لمتغيّر ما، أو مؤثر هيرميتي") makes the contradiction explicit, and line 464 tells the learner to think of this "متغيّر" as the Hamiltonian of a system. Correct renderings would be "مؤثر قابل للرصد" / "الكمية المرصودة". Secondary: "excited state" is consistently "حالة متحمِّسة" (= enthusiastic state) instead of the standard "حالة مثارة" (lines 372, 381, 430, 464, 472); "Deflation" in VQD is "الانحراف" (= deviation) rather than a deflation/reduction sense; and there are calques such as "سنستدعي الخطوات" for "call out the steps" (line 24) and "الحد الأدنى العالمي" for "global minimum" (line 608).

Beyond these, the "Check your understanding" label alternates between "تحقق من فهمك" (127, 658) and "اختبر فهمك" (518), and there are isolated minor grammar slips (line 224 "جزءًا ضئيلًا" accusative where the nominative subject is expected; line 274 gender-agreement "كانت...مجانية" for masculine "التحقق") and a slight softening of "exactly one of them contains a mine" at line 740 where "بالضبط" attaches to the verb rather than the count. tutorials/advanced-techniques-for-qaoa.m.review_opus_note_prior: The central problem name "max-cut" (the MAXIMUM-cut problem) is mistranslated and rendered inconsistently. In the most prominent places — the section heading (line 86) and the opening definition (lines 88-89) — it is "القطع الأصغر (max-cut)", which means "the SMALLER/minimum cut", the opposite of maximum cut. This produces a real contradiction for the learner: the section titled "the minimum-cut problem" immediately states its goal is to MAXIMIZE the edges between the two sets ("أقصى ما يمكن"). Worse, later in the same file (line 1001) the identical term is rendered correctly as "القطع الأقصى" (maximum cut), so the file calls the same concept both "minimum cut" and "maximum cut". The fix: render max-cut as "القطع الأقصى" consistently throughout (heading, definition, and line 1001). All other prose is faithful and natural (CVaR α=1 vs α=0 tradeoff, the 500-qubit scaling claim, the CVaR α-tail formula gloss, the eigenvalue cut-membership explanation), terminology is otherwise consistent (الكيوبتات, هاملتوني التكلفة, بوابات متبادلة for commuting gates, التغايري for variational), and informal register holds.

(1) The sentence defining the two topologically distinct ways a logical loop can wrap the torus collapses both into the same phrase: EN "around the hole in the middle of the torus, through it, or both" becomes "a través del agujero en el centro del toro, a través de él, o ambas cosas" — "around the hole" is mistranslated as "a través del agujero", so the Spanish offers "through the hole ... through it ... or both", which is self-contradictory and destroys the whole intuition for why the distance is L. (2) The EN author's explicit anti-misreading caveat defining what a lattice line is — "Here, a 'horizontal/vertical lattice line' means a full row/column of qubits in the periodic lattice (not the line segments of the loop of qubits affected by the X error)" — is dropped entirely from the Spanish, leaving the numbered loop taxonomy that immediately follows ambiguous in precisely the way the EN warns against. (3) Category 1's justification ("since each lattice line crosses the closed loop of errors once ... and once crossing back out") is compressed to a bare "(El ejemplo anterior entra en esta categoría.)", removing the parity argument that explains WHY the example is in the stabilizer. Additionally, "Such a loop of X errors" is rendered as "Una cadena de errores de este tipo" (chain, not loop) and EN's hedged "Perhaps more likely" is strengthened to a flat "es más probable".

learning/courses/general-formulation-of-.review_notes: Well-structured course intro
learning/courses/general-formulation-of-.review_opus_note: Second bullet inserts a qualifier the English does not have: "the state of one system that happens to be entangled with another system" becomes "el estado de un sistema que está *aleatoriamente* entrelazado con otro sistema". "Happens to be" is the idiomatic "resulta estar / da la casualidad de que está" — it marks an incidental circumstance, not randomness — whereas "aleatoriamente entrelazado" asserts *random* entanglement, narrowing the general motivation for reduced density matrices to an imagined special case, and it collides with the genuinely random notion in the preceding bullet ("estados cuánticos elegidos aleatoriamente"), so a learner is invited to read the two as the same phenomenon. Two smaller slips: in the opening sentence the parallel "represented ... represented" is broken ("los estados cuánticos se representan ... las operaciones se describen mediante matrices unitarias"), and "a critically important aspect" is calqued as "un aspecto fundamentalmente importante" where a native writer would say "de importancia fundamental" / "de una importancia crítica". Register (tú: "completa", "puedes abrir", "te guía") and core terminology (matrices de densidad, valores propios, aplicaciones lineales, matrices unitarias/estocásticas, entrelazado) are correct and consistent.

Notably the translator renders the identical hedge correctly at line 359 ("kemungkinan besar tidak mungkin" for "not likely to be possible"), proving this is an inconsistency, not a vocabulary gap; the fix is "kecil kemungkinannya" rather than "tidak mungkin" in both spots.

learning/courses/use-a-qc-today/quantum-.review_opus_note_prior: One genuine semantic inversion in the pedagogically critical "what quantum computing is NOT" myth-list. The English bullet "It is not useless until we achieve fault tolerance or error correction" debunks the myth (i.e. QC is already useful before fault tolerance). The Malay renders it "Ia tidak berguna sehingga kita mencapai toleran kesalahan atau pembetulan ralat", which reads naturally as "It is not useful until we achieve fault tolerance or error correction" — the exact OPPOSITE, re-asserting the very myth the list exists to dispel. Because "berguna" = useful, the negation now lands on the wrong word; it should be something like "Ia bukannya tidak berguna sehingga kita mencapai..." or "Ia tidak menjadi sia-sia/tidak berguna sehingga...". The rest of the file is meaning-faithful with consistent terminology (qubit, get, litar, Hamiltonian kept, pengoptimuman, pengurangan/pembetulan ralat, T_1/T_2 koherensi & dephasing), but this single inverted bullet would actively mislead a learner, which forces a FAIL.

guides/stretch.mdx.review_opus_note_prior: The core term "dynamical decoupling" is mistranslated as "dynamiczne sprzęganie" — but "sprzęganie" means *coupling*, the opposite of *decoupling* (correct Polish would be "odsprzęganie" / "rozprzęganie", or keeping "dynamical decoupling"). This inverts the concept: dynamical decoupling isolates/protects an idling qubit from noise, so telling a learner it is "coupling" teaches the reverse. The error recurs three times: the section heading "Dynamiczne sprzęganie" (line 19), "stosowanie dynamicznego sprzęgania do bezczynnego kubitu" (line 21), and "sekwencję XX dynamicznego sprzęgania" (line 23). It is also inconsistent with line 15, which keeps "echo decoupling" in English. Everything else in the file (stretch resolution, remainder/reszta handling, timing metadata explanation, Qiskit Runtime limitations) is faithful and reads naturally, and the informal "ty" register holds — but the decoupling→coupling inversion on the file's central example is a genuine domain-terminology error that misleads.

Two things a native technical editor would still change. First, the closing sentence of "O que é uma primitiva?" — "aproxima a programação quântica um passo a mais de onde a programação clássica está hoje" — is not idiomatic; "um passo a mais de onde" is a calque of "one step closer to where", and Portuguese wants "um passo mais perto de onde" / "aproxima mais um passo do ponto em que". Second, in the BaseEstimatorV1 bullet the English comparative "more commonly used" becomes the superlative "as mais comumente usadas", a small unwarranted strengthening of the claim about V2 primitives. Neither would give a learner a false idea of primitives.

guides/processor-types.mdx.review_opus_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every factual claim matches the source (120 qubits/r1 Nighthawk, 156/133 qubits Heron, dezembro de 2025, julho de 2024, "rede hexagonal pesada" for heavy-hex, "mitigação de TLS", "trocas entre diferentes atributos" for tradeoffs), and the informal "você" register holds in the Admonition. Two spots are stiff, calqued adjective placement that a native technical editor would reorder: in the Heron paragraph, "o controle de dois qubits e de qubit único rápido e de alta fidelidade" strands "rápido e de alta fidelidade" after "qubit único", so the qualifiers read as attaching only to single-qubit control instead of to the control as a whole; and in the Nighthawk paragraph "cargas de trabalho de aplicações aprimoradas" lets "aprimoradas" attach to "aplicações" rather than to the workloads, as in the English "enhanced application workloads". Neither would mislead a learner about the hardware — both are fluency/attachment slips, not meaning changes.

None of these would lead a learner to run the function incorrectly.

learning/courses/variational-algorithm-d.review_notes: Haiku linguistic review
learning/courses/variational-algorithm-d.review_opus_note: No hallucinations and no outright inverted claims — the ansatz/variational-form structure, the $D = 2^{2n}$ dimensionality argument, the three trade-offs (Bilis/Katumpakan/Ingay), and the N-local layer rules all survive intact, and the informal register holds throughout (no po/opo). What a native technical editor would fix is a cluster of ungrammatical focus/voice constructions that read as raw MT: "maaari kang subukan ng isang arbitrary na pamilya" (should be "maaari kang sumubok ng"/"maaari mong subukan ang"), "Maaari tayong ipasa ang ating mga data point" (should be "Maaari nating ipasa"), "Mayroon isang pundamental na trade-off" (missing linker: "Mayroong"), and "isang iba't ibang quantum state ang malilikha" ("iba't iba" = various, not "a different one"). Two word-level slips: "ilang mabait na mapping" renders "well-behaved mapping" with "mabait" (kind-hearted, of a person) instead of "maayos ang asal/kumikilos", and "pinaka-releban" is a malformed non-word for "pinakarelevante". Finally, "ang ika-0 qubit ay pinaka-malayo sa kanan" is ambiguous in Tagalog — the dominant reading is "farthest FROM the right", which risks teaching the opposite qubit ordering for the $ZZII$ string; "nasa pinakakanan" would be unambiguous. None of these rise to a false concept on their own, but together they are well past PASS.

However, the file contains a cluster of genuine semantic errors on the EVEN/ODD parity concept, which is load-bearing for Shor's algorithm. "Even number" ($N$ is even, line 47; the order $r$ is even, line 216) is rendered "pare-pareho" — which means "the same/consistent/equal," NOT even-parity — so the condition reads as nonsense to a learner. "Odd" ($N$ is odd, line 49; $r$ is odd, line 215) is rendered "kakaibang numero" = "strange/unusual number," a classic calque of the wrong sense of "odd." Worse, parity is rendered THREE inconsistent ways across the file: "pare-pareho" (47, 216), "kakaiba" for odd (49, 215), and "pantay" for even (True/False #5, line 819) — only "pantay" is correct. Step 3 of the algorithm ("Check if the order is even / If r is odd...") is therefore corrupted: a learner cannot correctly follow the parity branch. This is a meaning-level defect plus a ≥3-way within-file term inconsistency, so FAIL.

learning/courses/foundations-of-quantum-.review_opus_note_prior: Two core defined terms are systematically mistranslated in a way that misleads. (1) "non-identity Pauli matrices" is rendered "ненульові матриці Паулі" (= "non-zero") throughout (lines 16, 47, 50, 66, 86, 88, 101, 108, 164, 194, 237). The intended contrast is with the identity matrix $\mathbb{I}$ (rendered "одинична матриця" at line 16), so the correct term is "неодиничні"; "ненульові" tells the learner "non-zero", a different and vacuous condition (all Pauli matrices are non-zero), and breaks the central X/Y/Z-vs-identity distinction the lesson is built on. (2) "nondestructive(ly)" measurement is rendered "нерозкладальн-" (= "indecomposable / non-decomposable") throughout the final section and its heading (lines 218, 221/heading, 223, 232, 244, 252). The intended meaning is "неруйнівно" (without destroying/collapsing the state) — the whole point of the phase-estimation circuit. "нерозкладально" is the wrong concept (decomposition vs. destruction) and obscures the key pedagogical idea that the Bell state survives the $Z\otimes Z$ measurement. Apart from these two recurring term errors the prose is natural, faithful, and uses informal "ти" (lines 93-95, 227, 240).
